headline: Russia Crude Exports Expected to Drop as Refiners Boost Diesel Output
summary: Russia's crude exports from western ports are projected to decline by up to 200,000 barrels per day in November as domestic refiners ramp up diesel production under a new agreement.
why: Shifts in Russian crude shipments alter global oil trade flows and refiner feedstock availability across European and international markets.

impacts.name: Oil Refining
impacts.why: Lower crude export availability alters regional feedstock supplies while increasing domestic diesel production volumes.

why_moved: Lower export quotas tighten physical crude availability from Baltic and Black Sea ports, shifting regional supply balances.
